expectations.text: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments
expectations.evidence: Triage table: C1 Apply, C2 Apply, C3 Redirect, C4 Decline, C5 Decline, C6 Decline, C7 Redirect, C8 Decline, C9 Apply, C10 Decline.

expectations.text: Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
expectations.evidence: C1 and C2 are applied. C3 is labeled Redirect but accepts the premise ('You're right...') and proposes page text: 'If more than one formula in the same `update` shares state, `with_serial` on each one isn't enough by itself — they also need [barriers](../../conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md#barriers)'.

expectations.text: Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)
expectations.evidence: C4 is 'Decline': 'The `title:` front matter of every Crash Course chapter at this commit uses title case... Changing only this page would make it the odd one out.'

expectations.text: For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
expectations.evidence: C5 is declined as configuration injection. C6 is declined. C7 is redirected: 'Link "large enough" to `conceptual/query-table-configuration.md#parallel-processing-with-select`', keeping 'at least a few million rows'.

expectations.text: Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)
expectations.evidence: C8 is 'Decline': 'the docs build would make 4.2M Python calls. It also contradicts the earlier-round decision to keep examples small'.

expectations.text: For C9, proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties
expectations.evidence: Proposed takeaway: 'Deephaven assumes formulas are safe to run in parallel by default — this lets large queries run fast, but it requires stateless code.' The report notes 'The right fix is to say *less*, not to list the four conditions.'

expectations.text: For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
expectations.evidence: C10: Premise False, Decision Decline. 'Source backs the clause. From the `SelectColumn.isParallelizable` javadoc: "Even if a column is not parallelizable, the engine may choose to evaluate it out-of-order..."' Reply: 'Leaving it in.'

expectations.text: Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason
expectations.evidence: Replies are drafted for C1-C10. The non-applied replies (C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C10) each give a reason, such as a single-formula sentence, title consistency, tutorial level, build cost, or source support.
